newsitem.title: MEXICO: World Bank approves $186.5 mln loan for Mexico.
newsitem.headline: World Bank approves $186.5 mln loan for Mexico.

text.p: Mexico will receive a $186.5 million loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) for a federal water program, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
The loan, contracted by Mexico's national development bank Nacional Financiera, has a maturity of 15 years, including a grace period of three years, and an interest rate to be adjusted twice a year.
The statement said that the loan meets the federal government's limits for indebtedness for the fiscal year.

"The money will be distributed through Nacional Financiera and will be aimed at promoting the distribution of water in Mexico in an environmentally friendly and economically efficient manner," the ministry said in a statement.
Part of the government's water plan includes management of watersheds throughout the country and a program to promote dam safety, including an inspection program for dams taller than three meters.
The statement said the government will also study private sector help in water infrastructure projects.
